title: Boss: the deploy script review
summary: Parse arguments, model set -e, and plan log cleanup like a production script would.

steps.title: Code review
steps.body: A teammate's deploy script misbehaves. To review it properly you're going to model what bash actually does.

steps.title: Parse flags
prompt: Write `(Dictionary<string, string> Flags, List<string> Args) ParseArgs(List<string> argv)` handling the common script convention:
- a `--name` followed by nothing or by another `--flag` is a boolean: `Flags[name] = "true"`,
- `--` ends flag parsing: everything after it is a positional arg,
- anything else is a positional arg, in order.
starter: (Dictionary<string, string> Flags, List<string> Args) ParseArgs(List<string> argv)
solution: (Dictionary<string, string> Flags, List<string> Args) ParseArgs(List<string> argv)
hints: Use an index loop, so `--name value` can consume the next item with `++i`.
template: Dojo.Eq("--dry-run before another flag is boolean", "true", dojoF.GetValueOrDefault("dry-run"));
Dojo.Eq("--verbose takes the next positional", "api", dojoF.GetValueOrDefault("verbose"));

steps.title: What does set -e actually do?
prompt: Model a script. Each line is `(Cmd, Code)`: the command text and the exit code its **first** command would return. A line may be `"cmd || fallback"`, where the fallback always succeeds with code 0, unless the fallback is `exit N`. A command `exit N` ends the script with code N.

Write `(List<string> Ran, int Exit) RunScript(List<(string Cmd, int Code)> lines, bool errexit)` returning the commands that ran (the part before `||`, then the fallback if it ran) and the script's exit code:
- a failing command with no fallback stops the script with its code **only if** `errexit` (set -e); otherwise the script carries on,
- reaching the end gives exit code 0 (as if the last command succeeded; keep it simple).
starter: (List<string> Ran, int Exit) RunScript(List<(string Cmd, int Code)> lines, bool errexit)
solution: (List<string> Ran, int Exit) RunScript(List<(string Cmd, int Code)> lines, bool errexit)
if (bar >= 0) { first = cmd.Substring(0, bar); alt = cmd.Substring(bar + 4); }
hints: Handle `exit N` both as a command and as a fallback.
template: var dojoScript = new List<(string Cmd, int Code)> { ("cd /srv/app", 1), ("rm -rf build", 0), ("echo done", 0) };
Dojo.Eq("without -e it carries on in the wrong dir", new List<string> { "cd /srv/app", "rm -rf build", "echo done" }, dojoR1.Ran);
Dojo.Eq("with -e it stops", new List<string> { "cd /srv/app" }, dojoR2.Ran);
Dojo.Eq("with -e exit code is the failure", 1, dojoR2.Exit);
var dojoR3 = RunScript(new List<(string Cmd, int Code)> { ("grep -q x f || true", 1), ("cd /srv || exit 3", 2), ("echo never", 0) }, true);
Dojo.Eq("|| true and || exit N", new List<string> { "grep -q x f", "true", "cd /srv", "exit 3" }, dojoR3.Ran);

steps.title: Log rotation plan
prompt: The script's last job is cleaning `/var/log/app`. Write `List<string> RotationPlan(List<(string Name, int AgeDays)> files, int compressAfter, int deleteAfter)` that returns the commands it would run, sorted by file name (ordinal):
- `.log` files older than `compressAfter` days (but not deleted) → `gzip <name>`,
- anything else is left alone. "Older than" means strictly greater.
starter: List<string> RotationPlan(List<(string Name, int AgeDays)> files, int compressAfter, int deleteAfter)
solution: List<string> RotationPlan(List<(string Name, int AgeDays)> files, int compressAfter, int deleteAfter)
foreach (var (name, age) in files.OrderBy(f => f.Name, StringComparer.Ordinal))
hints: Sort first, then decide per file.
Check the delete rule before the compress rule.
template: var dojoFiles = new List<(string Name, int AgeDays)> { ("app.log", 0), ("app-0301.log", 3), ("app-0201.log", 40), ("app-0215.log.gz", 20), ("app-0101.log.gz", 70), ("README", 400) };
Dojo.Eq("plan", new List<string> { "rm app-0101.log.gz", "rm app-0201.log", "gzip app-0301.log" }, RotationPlan(dojoFiles, 1, 30));
